entries.appliesTo: licensed mental health professionals/providers and any individual, corporation, or entity offering therapy or psychotherapy services in Rhode Island

dutySources.disclosure-ui: § 40.1-5.5-3(a)(1)-(2) — 'the patient or the patient's parent, guardian or other legally authorized representative is informed in writing of the following… (1) That artificial intelligence will be used; (2) The specific purpose of the artificial intelligence tool or system that will be used'
dutySources.consent-workflow: § 40.1-5.5-3(a) — 'unless the patient or the patient's parent, guardian or other legally authorized representative is informed in writing of the following and provides consent as defined in § 40.1-5.5-2'
dutySources.human-review: § 40.1-5.5-3(c) — 'A licensed professional or provider may not allow or otherwise use artificial intelligence to do any of the following: (1) Make independent therapeutic decisions; … (3) Determine therapeutic recommendations or treatment plans.'

sources.aiTherapyRule: § 40.1-5.5-2(6) — ''Permitted use of artificial intelligence' means the use of artificial intelligence tools or systems by a licensed professional or provider to assist in providing administrative support or supplementary support in therapy or psychotherapy services where the licensed professional or provider maintains responsibility for clinical judgement and reasonable therapeutic oversight'
sources.consentRequired: § 40.1-5.5-3(a) — 'unless the patient or the patient's parent, guardian or other legally authorized representative is informed in writing of the following and provides consent as defined in § 40.1-5.5-2'
sources.scope: § 40.1-5.5-2(10) — ''Therapy or psychotherapy services' means services provided to diagnose or treat an individual's mental health or behavioral health.'
sources.enforcer: § 40.1-5.5-5(b) — 'The executive office of health and human services shall have authority to investigate any actual, alleged, or suspected violation of this chapter.' ; § 40.1-5.5-5(a) — 'The penalties pursuant to § 5-37.3-9 shall apply to any violation of the confidentiality provisions of this chapter.'

flags: aiTherapyRule=supervised is lossy: § 40.1-5.5-3(b) also bans standalone/direct-to-public AI therapy — 'may not provide, advertise, or otherwise offer therapy or psychotherapy services, including through the use of Internet-based artificial intelligence, to the public in this state unless the therapy or psychotherapy services are conducted by an individual who is a licensed professional or provider'

confidentiality duty fits no listed duty key: § 40.1-5.5-4 — 'All records kept by a licensed professional or provider and all communications… shall be confidential and shall not be disclosed except as provided pursuant to the provisions of § 40.1-5-26'
cross-referenced penalties reach only the confidentiality provisions, not the AI use restrictions; no penalty stated for violations of § 40.1-5.5-3

exemptions in § 40.1-5.5-5(c): religious counseling, peer support, public self-help/educational materials, FDA-cleared (or other federal agency-cleared) AI tools, and IRB-approved research under 21 C.F.R. Pt. 50 / 45 C.F.R. Pt. 46
